questions.q: What is the T-SQL-specific way to quote an identifier like a reserved word or a name with spaces?
options: Double quotes only, with no alternative
questions.explain: [Brackets] are the classic, always-available T-SQL quoting mechanism, independent of session settings.

questions.q: Under what condition can SQL Server also accept double-quoted identifiers like "Order"?
options: Only when the QUOTED_IDENTIFIER session setting is ON
Never — SQL Server only supports brackets
Only inside stored procedures, never in ad hoc queries
questions.explain: Double-quoted identifiers work on SQL Server only when QUOTED_IDENTIFIER is ON — a session setting that's on by default in most tools but can be off.

questions.q: What character does MySQL use by default to quote identifiers?
options: Double quotes ("identifier") by default, with no alternative
questions.explain: MySQL's default identifier-quoting character is the backtick; double quotes only work for identifiers if ANSI_QUOTES mode is enabled.

questions.q: What quoting style do Oracle and PostgreSQL share as their standard mechanism?
options: No quoting is supported on either platform
questions.explain: Both Oracle and PostgreSQL use standard ANSI double quotes to quote identifiers.

questions.q: What MySQL SQL mode setting makes double quotes work as identifier quotes instead of backticks?
questions.explain: ANSI_QUOTES is the MySQL SQL mode that enables double-quoted identifiers, though it's rarely enabled in real-world MySQL code.
